(redirects from owj0421/outfit-transformer; cloned 2026-10-03)
Vendored: 2026-10-03 (pristine upstream, unmodified — nested .git removed for a
plain-file vendor snapshot, exactly like vendor/fashn-vton-1.5 and
vendor/landmarks2anthropometry).

WHAT THIS IS (decision record)
  - Research implementation of "OutfitTransformer: Learning Outfit
    Representations for Fashion Recommendation" (Sarkar, Gao, V. Nagarajan,
    CVPRW 2022; extended WACV 2023). An outfit is an UNORDERED SET of items;
    self-attention over item embeddings produces an outfit token used for
    Compatibility Prediction (CP), and a target-item token used for
    Complementary Item Retrieval (CIR) / Fill-in-the-Blank (FITB) in a single
    step regardless of outfit length.
  - Used by Feature 06 (Outfit Builder) as the compatibility + FITB engine in
    `confit-outfit-worker` (Modal, CPU-only, scale-to-zero).
  - The deployed variant is OutfitCLIPTransformer (model_type="clip"):
    frozen FashionCLIP item encoder + 6-layer transformer head. Reported
    upstream performance: CP AUC 0.93 / FITB 67.02 (original);
    CP 0.95 / FITB 69.24 (+CLIP, SOTA) on Polyvore.
  - The item encoder is patrickjohncyh/fashion-clip — the SAME FashionCLIP
    already deployed in confit-tagging-worker (Feature 07), so Feature 06
    introduces NO new model family. The blueprint suggested reusing
    moda-embed embeddings, but the trained checkpoint requires its own
    FashionCLIP encoder space (aggregation='concat' of image+text); feeding
    moda-fashion-distilled vectors would be architecturally invalid. Deviation
    is deliberate and documented here.

WHY CPU-ONLY
  - ResNet/SentenceBERT-free CLIP variant is ViT-B/32 + a 6-layer transformer:
    inference is a few seconds per request on 2 vCPU. No GPU is burned for
    Feature 06 (standing constraint: GPU only where a model needs it).

LICENSE HONESTY
  - Upstream LICENSE: MIT (David Sarfati, Oshri Katzin, sagikeren3,
    bigohofone). Vendored code is MIT — commercial use OK.
  - FashionCLIP (patrickjohncyh/fashion-clip): MIT (Padora AI / patrickjohncyh,
    trained on Farfetch product data). Known bias: white-background product
    photos; disclosed in worker responses.
  - Trained on Polyvore outfits; scores are compatibility in the Polyvore
    fashion sense — the worker response carries this as a disclaimer.

TATTOO (benchmark pin — evaluation methodology only, NOT shipped as a model)
  - TATTOO: "Training-free AesTheTic-aware Outfit recOmmendation"
    (Wu, Hu, Zhou, Lu — arXiv:2509.23242). Pinned at build time as the
    type-aware evaluation rubric for Feature 06:
      * its aesthetic axes (color / style / occasion / season / material /
        balance) structure the worker's honest advisory `aesthetic_axes`
        block (CLIP text-anchor projection — a training-free profile in
        TATTOO's spirit, NOT the paper's MLLM pipeline; labeled as such);
      * its type-aware evaluation philosophy (does the model actually score
        type-consistent outfits above type-inconsistent ones?) is enforced
        by the deployed-worker validation suite
        (services/outfit-worker/tests/test_deployed_type_aware_eval.py).
